boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro: Study the graphs below, then answer the four questions that follow. In Gia’s performance the ensemble is made up of musicians on guitar, trumpet, drums and piano. The ensemble played three musical pieces (A, B and C). Each musical piece included at least one playing passage of each of the musicians. Each musician played at some times together with the others, at times alone and at times in parallel to other musicians. For each musician the graphs present the playing passages in the course of each piece (A, B or C). Each strip in the graphs describes one playing passage. The left edge of the strip indicates the point in time at which that playing passage began, and the length of the strip indicates the duration of the passage. The filling of the strip indicates whether the playing passage was pre-composed or whether it was improvised (see key). For example, in piece C, the trumpeter played a pre-composed passage immediately after another passage that was played before it. The improvised passage began 2 minutes after the beginning of the piece and lasted a minute. In parallel to that playing passage the guitarist also played.

Study the graphs below, then answer the four questions that follow. The graphs describe a college and the 6 departments of study in it. Some of the students in the college study in one department only, and the rest study in a combination of two departments. All the students in the college study in one of the years A, B or C. Each department in the college has a building. In the building a graph is presented that contains information about the department: the field of knowledge to which the department belongs (social sciences, natural sciences or humanities) and the number of students studying in the department, both in a division by years of study and the total of all of them (see key). If there are students studying in two departments, numbers appear on the line connecting the two buildings of the departments (the total of the students in all the departments includes them). The graphs also present the paths connecting the buildings and their lengths in metres (the paths are not drawn to scale). For example: in the physics department, which belongs to the natural sciences, 70 students study in total, of whom 10 in year A. Between the physics building and the literature building there is a path 100 m long.

questions.stem: Avinoam chose an even number, added 5 to it, multiplied by 3, and then subtracted 2. The number that will be obtained is necessarily –

methods.text: Track parity only. Even plus 5 is odd; odd times 3 stays odd; odd minus 2 is odd. So the result is necessarily odd.
Take \(x = 4\): \((4+5) \times 3 - 2 = 25\), which is odd, not prime, not divisible by 3 or 5 — one value kills the other three options.

questions.stem:
In a sack there are objects of several kinds: 6 red cubes, 3 yellow cubes, 4 red balls, and 2 yellow balls.
Orly takes one object out of the sack at random.

What is the chance that the object will be yellow?

Tal is older than Daniella by 24 years.  In another 8 years Tal will be twice as old as Daniella.

How old is Daniella today?

methods.text: \(T = D + 24\), and \(T + 8 = 2(D+8)\). Substituting gives \(D + 32 = 2D + 16\), so \(D = 16\).
\(D = 16\) makes Tal 40; in 8 years they are 24 and 48 ✓. One line per option.

questions.stem: The average of \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\) is greater than 8. The average of \(x\) and \(y\) is smaller than 8. Which of the following claims is necessarily correct?
options: None of the above claims is necessarily correct

questions.stem:
In the figure before you is a circle whose centre is \(O\).

According to this datum and the data in the figure, what is the ratio between the size of the dark area and the size of the hatched area?
\(x\) and \(y\) are two numbers from among the numbers 2, 3, 4. Given: \(x < y\) Which of the following possibilities is necessarily correct?
options: None of the three possibilities above is necessarily correct

methods.text: There are only three pairs. \(2^3 = 8 < 9 = 3^2\); \(2^4 = 16 = 4^2\); \(3^4 = 81 > 64 = 4^3\). All three relations occur, so none is necessary.
\(2^4 = 4^2\) is the pair worth knowing by heart — it is the only place where \(x^y = y^x\) with \(x \neq y\) in ordinary numbers, and it appears repeatedly in this section.

questions.stem:
Three workers of the printing machines in a set work at a fixed rate and one of them finishes the loading in 20 minutes.
Four workers who arrange the printouts in the set work at a fixed rate and one of them finishes the arranging in an hour.

How many hours will two workers need in order to empty the set and immediately afterwards arrange the printouts in it?

methods.text: Each loader alone takes 20 minutes, so three together take \(\frac{20}{3}\). Each arranger alone takes 60 minutes, so four together take 15.
Combine the two stages according to what the question asks — the two teams work on different tasks, so their times add rather than their rates.

questions.stem: The total duration of the improvised playing passages of ____ in all three pieces together was two and a half minutes.
How many of the musicians played in piece A, also in piece B and also in piece C at the point in time that fell \(3\dfrac{1}{4}\) minutes after the beginning of the piece?

During one of the pieces a member of the audience left the hall at the moment at which exactly two of the musicians were playing improvised. Therefore, it is not possible that the member of the audience left ____ minutes after the beginning of that same piece.
A piece ends at the moment at which the last playing passage in it ends. In which of the pieces did the guitarist play an improvised playing passage during the last half minute of the piece?
options: In none of the three pieces

Efrat, Beni and Gilad had equal sums of money. Efrat gave to Beni half of the sum of money she had. Afterwards Beni gave to Gilad half of the sum of money he had. Finally Gilad gave to Efrat half of the sum of money he had. Now, whose sum of money out of the three is the smallest?
options: Now the sums of money of all three of them are equal to one another

methods.text: Give each 1 unit. Efrat halves: \(0.5, 1.5, 1\). Beni halves his: \(0.5, 0.75, 1.75\). Gilad halves his: \(1.375, 0.75, 0.875\).
Beni ends smallest. Tracking all three columns at once, rather than one person, is what keeps the sequence straight.

questions.stem: What is the smallest positive number of which 3% is a whole number?

methods.text: \(3\%\) of \(n\) is \(\frac{3n}{100}\), which is whole when 100 divides \(3n\). Since 3 and 100 share no factor, the smallest positive \(n\) need not be whole itself — \(n = \frac{100}{3}\) gives exactly 1.
\(33\frac13\): \(3\%\) of it is 1 ✓. \(12\frac12\) gives \(0.375\), 30 gives \(0.9\), and 100 gives 3 — whole, but larger.

questions.stem:
In the figure before you \(ABC\) is a right-angled triangle, and \(EBFD\) is a rectangle.

Given:  \(BF = 2\) cm ,  \(FC = x\) cm

What is the length of \(AE\) (in cm)?

Given:  \(-\dfrac{1}{2} < \dfrac{1}{x} < \dfrac{1}{2}\) ,  \(x \ne 0\)

What is the exact range of the values of \(x\)?

methods.text: Do not multiply by \(x\) — its sign is unknown, so you cannot know whether to flip. Read it as size instead: \(\left|\frac1x\right|<\frac12\) means \(|x|>2\), which is two rays.
Handle the two halves separately. For \(x>0\), \(\frac1x<\frac12\) gives \(x>2\). For \(x<0\), \(-\frac12<\frac1x\) gives \(x<-2\). Union the two cases.
\(x=3\) satisfies the given (\(\frac13\) is inside the band) and \(x=1\) does not (\(1\) is outside it). So small values are excluded and large ones included — which only option (1) manages.

questions.stem:
It is known that the human eye distinguishes between two points only if the distance between them is 0.1 mm at the least.
One wishes to draw a map of some area, and in it two buildings the distance between which is 5 metres.

What is the smallest scale of the map in which it will be possible to distinguish between the two buildings?

methods.text: 5 metres is 5,000 mm. For the gap to be at least 0.1 mm on the map, the scale factor can be at most \(\frac{5000}{0.1} = 50{,}000\).
“Smallest scale” means the most zoomed out, which is the largest denominator — the wording is the whole difficulty.

questions.stem: The operation \(\$\) is defined for every whole and positive number \(n\) thus: \(\$(n) = \) (the sum of the digits of \(n\)) Given: \(a\) and \(b\) are whole and positive numbers. Claim I: if \(a < b\), then \(\$(a) < \$(b)\) Claim II: \(\$(a+b) = \$(a) + \$(b)\) Which of the claims is necessarily correct?
Given: the volume of cube B is larger by a factor of 2 than the volume of cube A. By what factor is the surface area of cube B larger than that of cube A?
There is a department belonging to ____ in which exactly \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) of the students study in year ____.

A path connecting two buildings directly will be called “unused” if there are no students studying in a combination of the two departments that the path connects.

What is the total length of all the unused paths?

A lecturer left the physics department building and began to walk along the paths of the college. She passed through each one of the buildings of the college exactly once. It is not possible that the last building she reached was the building of the ____ department.

It is known that in year C there is no student studying in the philosophy department who also studies in an additional department. Therefore, the number of students in year A in the philosophy department who combine studies in an additional department is at least ____ and at most ____.
\(12\cdot\left(\dfrac{1}{6} - \dfrac{3}{4}\right) = ?\)

methods.text: Distribute before subtracting: \(12 \cdot \frac16 = 2\) and \(12 \cdot \frac34 = 9\), so the value is \(2-9 = -7\).

questions.stem:
At the beginning of the month the price of a sweater was 100 shekels.  In the middle of the month its price rose by \(k\%\).
At the end of the month the price rose a second time, this time by 20%, and reached 132 shekels.

\(k = ?\)

methods.text: \(k=10\): 100 rises to 110, then 20% more is 132 ✓. Dividing by the known 20% step first is quicker than expanding.
The numerator and denominator share the factor \((3x+4)\), so the fraction is \(\frac{3x-4}{3x+4}\). Setting that equal to 2 gives \(3x-4 = 6x+8\), so \(x = -4\).
Substituting \(x=-4\): the fraction is \(\frac{-16}{-8} = 2\) ✓. Option (3) is the value that makes the denominator zero — the excluded value offered as an answer.

questions.stem:
Given a square whose area is 32 sq.cm.

What is the length of the diagonal of this square (in cm)?

Given:

\(a < b\)
\(|b| < |a|\)

\((a, b \ne 0)\)

Which of the following claims follows from the data?
options: \(a\) can be negative or positive, and \(b\) can be negative or positive
\(a\) can be negative or positive, and \(b\) is necessarily positive
\(a\) is necessarily negative, and \(b\) can be negative or positive

methods.text: \(a<b\) says \(a\) is to the left; \(|b|<|a|\) says \(a\) is further from zero. Both can only be true if \(a\) is negative — a positive number to the left of \(b\) would be closer to zero, not further.
\(b\) is genuinely free. \(a=-5,\ b=2\) satisfies both givens with \(b\) positive, and \(a=-5,\ b=-2\) satisfies them with \(b\) negative. That kills every option that pins \(b\).

questions.stem: The width of a building's room is 5 metres, and its length is 9 metres. One wishes to tile the room with square tiles the length of whose side is 1 metre. The colour of the tiles adjacent to the walls is grey, and the rest of the tiles are white. How many white tiles were used in tiling the room?

The letters \(A\) and \(B\) represent digits between 1 and 9, so that \(AB\), for example, is a two-digit number whose tens digit is \(A\).

Given:

\(\begin{array}{r}A1\\ \times\ A1\\ \hline 1BB\end{array}\)

\(A + B = ?\)

methods.text: Write the two-digit number by place value: \(\overline{A1} = 10A + 1\), so the product is \((10A+1)^2 = 100A^2 + 20A + 1\). The units digit is 1 whatever \(A\) is, and the size of \(A\) decides how many digits the answer has.

With a three-digit result, only \(A = 1, 2, 3\) are possible, giving \(121\), \(441\) and \(961\). Match each against the pattern \(\overline{1BB}\) — the hundreds digit must be 1 and the last two digits equal.

In the figure before you \(AB\) is a diameter in a circle whose centre is \(O\).
\(a\) and \(b\) are straight lines tangent to the circle at points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively.
\(CD\) is tangent to the circle at point \(E\).

According to these data and the data in the figure,

\(\delta = ?\)
Which of the following expressions is a whole number?
options: None of the above expressions is a whole number

methods.text: A fraction is a whole number only if every prime in the denominator appears in the numerator. Each option puts a prime downstairs that is absent upstairs.
\(\frac{2^5 3^5}{5}\) has no 5 on top; \(\frac{2^6 5^3}{3}\) has no 3; \(\frac{3^2 5^4}{2}\) has no 2. All three fail, so the answer is none of them.

questions.stem: In a certain class the average of the Bible grades was 80. After Daniel joined the class the average rose to 80.5. It is known that Daniel's grade in Bible is 96. How many pupils were in the class after Daniel joined?

Two straight lines are drawn in a rectangle: one connects the two long sides of the rectangle, and the other connects the two short sides of the rectangle.  The straight lines do not pass through the vertices of the rectangle.  The rectangle is cut along these straight lines and four quadrilaterals are obtained.

At least one of these quadrilaterals must be –
options: The quadrilaterals do not have to be any of the above shapes

questions.stem: Rachel and Hodaya are playing in a competition. Hodaya starts running first. Rachel waits 20 seconds and then chases after Hodaya along the same route. Each of them runs at a fixed speed throughout the game. By what factor must Rachel's speed be greater than Hodaya's speed in order for her to catch up with her after 30 seconds from the beginning of the game?

methods.text: Careful with the clock: the 30 seconds is measured from the start of the game, so Hodaya runs 30 seconds and Rachel only 10.
Equal distances at the catch-up: \(30h = 10r\), so \(r = 3h\). Reading the 30 seconds as Rachel's own running time gives \(\frac32\), which is option (1) — the trap.

questions.stem:
Given:  \(n\) is a whole number greater than 2.

Which of the following values can be the value of the expression \(\dfrac{(n+1)!}{(n-2)!\cdot n}\)?

methods.text: Expand the top down to \((n-2)!\): \((n+1)!=(n+1)\,n\,(n-1)\,(n-2)!\). Everything cancels except \(\dfrac{(n+1)\,n\,(n-1)}{n}=(n+1)(n-1)=n^2-1\).
So the question is which option is one less than a perfect square. \(21\), \(54\) and \(70\) are not; \(35=36-1\) is, with \(n=6\). Recognising the shape \(n^2-1\) turns four candidates into one.

In the eighties a town was established, and in it houses of three kinds were built, all of them having one storey and without parking. In the nineties the council permitted residents to expand their houses in one of two ways: to add to them a second storey, or to add to them an attic storey (the council did not permit adding both a second storey and an attic). In the two thousands the council permitted residents to add parking to their houses, if they wished to. Apart from this, the council's policy has not changed from then until today. How many kinds of houses are possible in the town today?
